newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thailand will push back more than 100,000 ethnic minority refugees to Burma as soon as fighting in the country subsides, according to a resolution made yesterday at a National Security Council (NSC) meeting. Army chief and the interior minister, which is responsible for overseeing refugee affairs, confirmed the NSC's drastic decision to repatriate the refugees, mainly Karen and Karenni groups. (THE NATION)

- The chief of the Criminal Court has ordered an internal investigation after a key heroin trafficking suspect, allegedly involved in the biggest heroin shipment ever to the United States, is reported to have jumped bail. Despite special surveillance and repeated warnings from Thai and anti-drug authorities, Li Yun Chung, or Phongsak Rojganasakkul, failed to report to court on March 7 after being granted bail of five million baht on February 7. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- The opposition has jumped at Deputy Prime Minister Samak Sundaravej's call for a special House session to debate the Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) scam, but raises doubts about how serious he is in making the proposal. Democrat leader Chuan Leekpai has challenged the government to call an extraordinary House session to debate the BBC scandal in which MPs from both camps were allegedly involved. (BANGKOK POST)

- Don Muang's place as Thailand's number one airport is apparently assured with the news that the board of New Bangkok International Airport, the second Bangkok international airport (SBIA) operating body, has decided to cut its initial annual capacity by half, to 15 million from 30 million passengers. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thailand's commerce and foreign ministers are paying a rare joint visit to Vietnam today in a bid to forge new trade and economic ties. Major topics on the ministers' agenda are resolving disputes over territorial waters used by fishermen from both countries, and overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand. (BANGKOK POST)
